appraisal_events.evidence: il n'y a pas de supplice que je ne m'imposerais pour que la vieille bête me présentât à l'auteur de la sonate
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann declares he would endure any torment to be introduced to the sonata's author, an exaggerated expression of reverence for the composer's genius.

appraisal_events.evidence: Comment, s'écria Mme Verdurin, il y a encore des gens qui se font soigner par Potain !
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin dismisses Potain as passe, mocking anyone who still consults him, though Cottard mildly defends him as one of his own masters.

appraisal_events.evidence: Le peintre avait entendu dire que Vinteuil était menacé d'aliénation mentale... on pouvait s'en apercevoir à certains passages de sa sonate.
appraisal_events.explanation: A rumor that Vinteuil's incipient mental instability can be detected in his sonata subtly discredits his genius; Swann's troubled reaction shows the suggestion lands rather than being dismissed as absurd.

status_effects.explanation: Swann's hyperbolic willingness to suffer any torment to meet him marks strong reverence for the composer's genius.
The rumored hint of madness detectable in his sonata complicates and slightly undercuts his reputation.
Mme Verdurin's mockery casts him as an outdated choice of doctor.

ambiguities: Swann frames the object of his admiration ('l'auteur de la sonate') and the dismissed acquaintance ('la vieille bête') as possibly distinct people related by family, so it is unclear whether both references resolve to the same Vinteuil entity used here.
